name: Transfer Pricing
title: Transfer Pricing
answer: Transfer pricing is the practice of setting and defending the prices charged for goods, services, intangibles and financing between related entities in different tax jurisdictions. It sits inside corporate tax and jurisdictional compliance because the same transaction can be priced differently under the rules of each country involved. The work covers policy design, documentation, benchmarking against comparable transactions, and support during audits and dispute resolution. It applies to multinational groups of any size, though the compliance burden scales with the number and complexity of intercompany flows.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Transfer pricing is the practice of setting and defending the prices charged for goods, services, intangibles and financing between related entities in different tax jurisdictions. It sits inside corporate tax and jurisdictional compliance because the same transaction can be priced differently under the rules of each country involved. The work covers policy design, documentation, benchmarking against comparable transactions, and support during audits and dispute resolution. It applies to multinational groups of any size, though the compliance burden scales with the number and complexity of intercompany flows.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Practitioners work from the group's legal entity structure, intercompany agreements, trial balances and segmented financial data, usually pulled from the ERP and consolidation systems. Benchmarking relies on commercial databases of comparable company and transaction data, alongside public filings and, where relevant, customs valuation records. Documentation is assembled in a document management system and increasingly in a dedicated transfer pricing platform that links policies, agreements and calculations. Spreadsheets remain common for local file calculations, and tax authority portals handle filing and exchange of country by country reports.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The core method is functional analysis: establishing what each entity does, what assets it uses and what risks it bears, then selecting a method that fits, such as comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, transactional net margin or profit split. Comparables are screened for similarity and adjusted for differences in working capital, risk and accounting treatment. The resulting margin or price range is tested against the group's actual results, and adjustments are made where the outcome falls outside the range. Documentation is refreshed annually, and the analysis is revisited when the business model, supply chain or market conditions change.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Transfer pricing sits under the OECD guidelines and the UN manual, applied through each country's domestic law, with the arm's length principle as the common standard. The main instruments are the master file, local file and country by country report, filed under local deadlines and exchanged between tax authorities. Penalties, interest and double taxation are the practical risks, and mutual agreement procedures or advance pricing arrangements are the routes to relief. Records must be retained and defensible, and the analysis should reflect what the business actually did rather than what was planned.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more standardised reporting, more data exchange between authorities and more scrutiny of intangibles and profit allocation, particularly under the two pillar framework. Automation is moving into comparables selection, margin monitoring and documentation drafting, which shifts the practitioner's time toward judgement and audit defence. Disputes are likely to remain the pressure point, so groups are investing in contemporaneous evidence and clearer intercompany agreements. The practical test for any tool or process is whether it produces a defensible position that holds up under review.
